newsitem.title: USA: Nelson Gold says Zeravshan operation halted.
newsitem.headline: Nelson Gold says Zeravshan operation halted.

text.p: Nelson Gold Corp Ltd said on Thursday the mining and milling operations of the Zeravshan Gold Co would be halted indefinitely.

Zeravshan Gold's operations will be placed on care and maintenance, pending resolution of the current impasse on outstanding issues with the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan and the sale of gold by Zeravshan Gold, it said.

Commonwealth and British Minerals Ltd, a 100 percent-owned subsidiary of Nelson Gold, is manager and operator of and holds a 49 percent stake in Zeravshan Gold. The Tajik Government holds a 51 percent stake.
Nelson Gold, through Commonwealth and British Minerals has invested $54 million in Zeravshan Gold.

International Finance Corp representatives are participating in the discussions with Commonwealth and British Minerals and the Tajik Government in an effort to resolve the outstanding issues of the refining of gold, fiscal conditions, and joint venture refinements.

An agreement was reached on June 17, 1996 with the Tajik Government in the form of a protocol. However, the company said that various deadlines for the implementation of the protocol by the Tajik Government were not met.
As a consequence, refined and dore gold held in Tajikistan of 25,000 ounces with a current value $9.5 million remain unsold. Mining and milling operations would be halted on October 31, it said.
